properties.decision:
ANTHONY'S CHOICE, 2026-08-10: "let's go with D, then a small addition, then B." Three steps in order, and the ordering is the substance — each one is cheap only because the one before it has landed.

STEP 1 — STOP SERIALIZING DEFAULTS (option D, `fact:bl-198`). Do not write a property value equal to the schema default, so an ABSENT property honestly means "nobody said". Partly landed already: 0.25.0 wrote defaults into the export and 0.27.0 does not, while BL-198 is still listed PLANNED in `epoch:planned-one-write-surface` — so part of this step is reconciling the plan with what shipped rather than building.

THE REASON THIS ORDERING PUTS D FIRST AND DROPS C, and it is the load-bearing argument: D DELIVERS C'S SEMANTICS DERIVATIONALLY. Option C was "give a property difference provenance so a default never reads as a change". BL-198's own fix shape already produces exactly that — presence means somebody said it, absence means nobody did — without storing a second provenance field, which is the form `dec:certainty-derived` insists on for requirement certainty and the same argument applies here. C is therefore NOT rejected on merit; it is rendered unnecessary by D, and stays on `dec:idea-does-a-session-open-by-comparing-the-record` in case something after D still cannot be answered.

STEP 2 — A COMPARISON DISCLOSES ITS OWN CONFOUND (the addition, not among the five options). Every export carries `reflow2_version` in its stamp. When two records being compared were written by different builds, the comparison SAYS SO and says that property-only differences may be attributable to that. This is the one change that would have prevented both false claims: 2026-08-08 and 2026-08-10 were both cross-build comparisons, and neither reader could see the confound. It is DISCLOSURE, not a threshold — the same move `propose_heal` makes when it says "the alphabet chose the victim", and deliberately NOT the rejected option of tuning severity until phantoms fall below it, which silences true and false findings at the same rate.

IT IS ALSO WHAT D DOES NOT FIX. Suppressing defaults cleans the steady state and MOVES the disagreement to the version transition — every upgrading consumer meets it once. Step 2 is what makes that meeting survivable, which is why it follows D rather than replacing it.

STEP 3 — THE LOOP SAYS WHAT DISTRIBUTION IS OWED (option B, flo2's F5). Extend the read-side hint chosen in `dec:read-hint-shape` (state-derived, riding orientation reads, fire-on-change) to carry "the live graph and the committed record disagree" alongside coherence debt. LAST ON PURPOSE: a hint that fires on phantom findings teaches the agent to skim it, which would damage the one mechanism that currently earns attention — the exact failure `dec:read-hint-shape` rejected option B for. Its value is entirely downstream of the finding deserving belief.

WHAT WAS NOT CHOSEN. (A) do nothing — the null option, and it was a real candidate: `where-am-i` already prescribes the comparison and what failed was belief, not compliance. Rejected because the record was wrong on main for an unknown number of PRs and `reflow2_check` structurally cannot notice, reading checksums and anchored gaps and never properties. (E) move the trigger to publish time — not rejected on merit, merely not now: it cannot catch what is already committed and wrong, which was the observed case, and it inherits the same confound until step 2 lands. It becomes nearly free afterwards.

THE QUESTION THIS ANSWERS was NOT "when should the comparison run". It was "what has to be true before running it earlier makes anyone better off", and all three steps are about making the instrument believable rather than about scheduling it. Whether it then becomes a session's opening move is left genuinely open on the superseded idea node.
properties.name: Fix the comparison before pointing it earlier — stop serializing defaults, then disclose build skew, then report distribution debt
properties.rationale:
Recorded as a decision rather than left on the brainstorm node because Anthony chose, and `dec:governance-integrates-not-splits` set the precedent two days earlier for exactly this shape: a new accepted Decision OBSOLETES the brainstormed one, which goes `superseded` with all its options intact rather than being edited into an answer. The roads not taken keep their reasoning that way, and C in particular is worth being able to find again — it is superseded by an argument (D subsumes it) rather than by a judgement, and if that argument fails C is still there.

The measurements this rests on are recorded separately and independently: `fact:bl-198-cost-measured-twice-in-both-directions` (why the instrument is not believable) and `fact:orphan-decision-is-silenced-by-an-edge-that-does-not-reach-it` (found while checking this session's own work). Both carry their own counter-arguments, so a later session can attack the evidence without having to attack the decision.

Step 2 is mine rather than Anthony's and is marked as such: it was not one of the five options put to him, and he adopted it on the argument that it is the smallest change that would have caught both incidents.
